title: Freddie's drinking, Manuel's temperance and a dead bassist's wake
summary: Freddie got along with drinkers; Manuel Perez never drank and died; Keppard looks at bassist Joe Morris at his wake.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah. You see? Just too busy running around. That's right. Right. That's right. Some people talk like you, you talk like you started hard to get along with, because he was your brother, but do you think other people got along with him fast? They always liked him. They were like you said, they were funny.

Well I'll tell you, people got along with Freddie if they could drink. Yeah. And if they drink whiskey, then good whiskey. But if they never had, if they never drank whiskey they couldn't get along with him. Well one fella could get along with him and that would make him be his best friend, Manny Monero. Now I can tell you he drinks no. That's swelling taking place. Now of course they tell me he don't drink much.

But you know he used to drink though, didn't he? He does so. Yeah, he used to, he come to wakes right here, stop right there. And he will spend his money on it. Yeah. He'll get a half a pint of a pint, get it there. And he say and give him, what they call again, some, is it setting up or something he wants to chase him. Yeah, yeah. He'll stand up right there and drink every bit of it. And he step up another fella drinking, he stand up right there and go home just as sober as me or you. I'm telling you, I see him stay there and drink and get some more. And go home and don't ask nobody to bring him home. The next time I see him, he's just as straight as a picket. Of course I understand there's a time for everything. You know, he could be eating on the inside. But of course he don't feel it now. But maybe in a lifetime he will feel it. Well, we just, what the look of my prayers, he nobody drink. I played with Manuel. I played with him about, say about a year or something, him and Vic, old Gaspar. You heard of him talking about Vic Gaspar, the tramo player. Of course the boarder was dead now, I believe. Well, Vic was the tramo player and Oak was the bass player. Well, Manuel never drink. Manuel never bummed. Manuel never smoked. First he get through playing as a horny hall anywhere else. He was like a Mexican fella. When he got through, he went home. Never drink, never bummed, never drank, never done nothing. Now I went home. He turned right around and he died. Yeah, that's right.
You can't tell what's going to kill you.

It's no use. When you've got to die, you've got to die. It's no use. And it's no use to cry. See, like some time I got in the wake, I said, well, I said, you know, I looked down at a fellow, they had a fellow died the other day. I didn't know him. They say he used to play bass.
Oh, Joe Morris, well I didn't know him. I went and looked at him unless I seen him so long. He was right down low pace. Oh yes.
I didn't know him, no. Once we, I know Slowdrag bought his bass in 1945. Yeah, well they say he gave up music. He gave up music.

They tell me he used to play with Sam, Sam Morgan and Chris Kelly. Might have been, I don't know who he was. I don't know, but I told all the people. I went and looked at him. You didn't know him? No, my wife said go and see the father. I said, I'll say no.
